title: Finite Q3 unitary-history tail Holder corollary
question: For unitary Q3 character histories, can the inverse-free sandwiched Holder envelope remove all history-side L4 factors and leave only one cutoff-tail fourth-moment factor?
method: Use the finite Gibbs density rho and S=rho^(1/4) for the declared Q3 volumes 2, 4, and 6 and beta values 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, and 2.

For both cutoff orientations, all interpolation values, both positive times, and each cutoff radius, evolve the unitary configuration character with the finite perturbed Hamiltonian and form W as the self-adjoint cutoff tail.

Check the unitary identities and the exact normalized-state relation ||S||_4=1. Apply finite Schatten Holder to S[W,A_t]S=(SW)(A_tS)-(SA_t)(WS), so the history legs are at most one; check the stronger reduced bound N2_sym([W,A_t])<=2||SW||_4 and the adjoint-history version.

Check the self-adjoint tail left/right fourth-leg equality, measure source and disjoint-tail commutators, reconstruct all rows in a non-importing independent lane, and compile Lean R347 for the scalar corollary.
finding: Primary 851/851 and independent 851/851 pass. The integrated verifier passes 14/14 with Lean R347 PASS. All 360 finite history rows and both adjoint orientations satisfy the reduced inverse-free Holder bound. The largest lhs/(2 tail-leg) ratio is 0.04193148910394488, the largest tail fourth-leg factor is 3.9249685856134424, the largest reduced envelope is 7.849937171226885, and the largest sandwich lhs is 0.11986154052772928. History-side L4 factors stay at 1 within numerical tolerance for every normalized unitary history. The volume maxima of the tail leg are 1.4937084146969866 at V=2, 3.9249685856134424 at V=4, and 1.6042066149714334 at V=6; beta maxima decrease from 3.9249685856134424 at beta=0.125 to 1.2007925110524327 at beta=2. Source and disjoint-tail commutators remain below 7.82258885373977e-15 and 3.2040556572188632e-15.
decision_reason: The unitary specialization is a genuine reduction of the prior four-leg Holder expression: normalized unitarity removes the history-dependent L4 factors exactly, and self-adjointness removes the two distinct tail-leg values up to the tested finite trace identity. Thus the direct Duhamel route has one explicit remaining state-weighted tail quantity. Its finite beta/volume dependence, finite oscillator truncation, and lack of cutoff removal mean that no common-core uniform estimate is closed and no no-go is inferred.
closed: finite inverse-free reduced Holder envelope for both orientations and adjoints
finite actual-Q3 history and support rows
open: source-, volume-, cutoff- and beta-uniform local tail fourth-moment estimate on a named unbounded Q3 common core
continuity of the tail four-point Euclidean form under oscillator-cutoff and spatial-exhaustion limits
modular-domain transfer and direct D,delta-D Cauchy
all-shape exhaustion, product/core density and common alpha
Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification and a phasewise GNS gap
continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A

adversarial_review.check: Every history and adjoint is checked against both U*U=I and UU*=I before the L4 reduction is used.
The Gibbs probabilities are normalized and ||rho^(1/4)||_4 is checked against one; no partition-function factor is omitted.
The tail is explicitly symmetrized and the left/right fourth-leg equality is checked without commuting it through rho.
The factors remain SW, A_tS, SA_t, and WS in the Holder products; only unitary norm invariance is used.
Only a positive quarter root is formed, so the reduced corollary has no finite Gibbs inverse or spectral-floor hypothesis.
Numerical root and unitarity residuals are reported as finite diagnostics and are not interpreted as infinite-dimensional domain control.
The tail leg varies across beta and volume; the finite maxima are not promoted to a uniform local moment theorem.
The oscillator dimensions are the declared finite fixtures and no exact CCR or common unbounded core is claimed.
The independent lane reconstructs all model and singular-value calculations without importing the primary lane.
R347 checks scalar nonnegative assembly only; matrix Holder, Gibbs spectral calculus and limits remain outside Lean.
The result does not close the local tail moment, direct Cauchy, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A gates.

qft_interface.closed: For normalized unitary finite Q3 histories, the Holder integrand reduces to the single self-adjoint cutoff-tail fourth-leg factor, uniformly in history time and interpolation at fixed finite state.
qft_interface.open: The tail fourth-leg factor still needs a local source/volume/cutoff/beta-uniform common-core estimate and cutoff/exhaustion continuity before direct Duhamel, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A promotion.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 finite evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner or physical-empty comparison is supplied.

next_action: Express the tail fourth-leg factor as a two-slice Euclidean local correlation and derive a coercive local moment bound uniform in spatial volume and oscillator cutoff on the declared Q3 common core; test the first cutoff-growth obstruction if the bound cannot be obtained.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Q3 unitary-history Holder corollary. It is not a thermodynamic common-Hilbert theorem, a common-alpha construction, a mass-gap proof, a continuum result, or a QFT/Clay closure.
no_overclaim: This record promotes only the finite normalized-unitary reduction and tail-leg identity. It does not prove tail moment uniformity, unbounded-domain transfer, direct Cauchy convergence, exhaustion independence, common alpha, Hamiltonian-OS identification, a GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.
